candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Find a common denominator and rewrite fractional parts as equivalent fractions before subtracting when the original denominators differ.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S01 and C.S01 are essentially identical in name and definition. B.S01 overlaps strongly on common-denominator conversion; although it also includes rewriting a whole number as a whole plus 0/d, its core operation is still matching fraction units via common denominators, so it aligns best here.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract fractions with a common denominator and/or subtract the whole-number and fractional parts of mixed numbers once the quantities are in compatible form.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts include a direct subtraction skill performed after forms are aligned. The wording is nearly identical across A.S02, B.S03, and C.S03.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a whole number or nonstandard mixed number into a subtraction-ready form, such as adding a zero fractional part or converting an improper mixed number to a standard mixed number.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: B.S02 and C.S02 clearly cover normalization/preparation rewrites before subtraction. A.S03 is broader because it also includes borrowing/regrouping, but part of its definition explicitly matches this normalization concept, including normalizing improper mixed-number parts and rewriting whole numbers with fractional parts.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Borrow 1 whole and convert it into fractional units to continue subtraction when the fractional part of the minuend is too small.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: Borrowing/regrouping is explicitly present in B.S04 and C.S04 as a distinct operation. A does not isolate borrowing separately; it embeds it inside A.S03 together with normalization, so no separate A-only skill maps uniquely to this concept without violating one-to-one assignment of skill IDs.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the result to lowest terms and express it appropriately as a fraction, mixed number, whole number, or zero.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S04 isolates final simplification and expression as its own skill. In B and C, simplification is bundled together with regrouping in B.S04 and C.S04 rather than separated into a standalone skill, so no distinct B or C skill maps exclusively to this concept.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks share strong agreement on common-denominator conversion and direct subtraction after alignment. The main structural difference is granularity around preparatory rewriting, borrowing, and simplification: A separates simplification but combines normalization with borrowing, while B and C separate normalization from subtraction but combine borrowing with simplification. Every skill ID was mapped exactly once, with broad concepts aligned where experts differed in how finely they split the work.
